newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope discusses N.Ireland with President Robinson.
newsitem.headline: Pope discusses N.Ireland with President Robinson.

text.p: Pope John Paul discussed the social and economic situation in Ireland and the Northern Irish question with President Mary Robinson at an audience at the Vatican on Saturday.
Chief Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls told reporters the two discussed "defence and promotion of spiritual values" in Roman Catholic Ireland and the problems of the family.

Irish couples were allowed to file for divorce for the first time last month following an historic 1995 referendum which split the country and scrapped the ban on divorce by less than one percentage point. The Vatican is opposed to divorce.
Navarro-Valls said the audience also focused on the peace process in Northern Ireland, where Irish republican guerrillas are fighting to end British rule. He gave no details of their talks.
Robinson, Ireland's first woman president, is on an official visit to Italy and on Friday addressed a ceremony at the U.N.'s World Food Programme in honour of International Women's Day.
